items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: I didn’t play well at all with that. Especially when Duke was conducting... I was not successful with that band.

ctx.x: Now you made a comment that you felt you didn’t play good with Ellington ‘cause you were listening too hard.

No I didn’t play well with that thing, no, I didn’t play well at all with that. Especially when Duke was conducting. He goes like this you know. He looked like a knuckle ball © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

pitcher up there, you wonder when he’s going to let the band start coming in. I didn’t know what he was doing. When Harry Carney beat off the tempo, I sounded like a million bucks with those guys. You know, he’d just go one, two, three, four, and man in you go. But Duke was like, whew, like whirling dervish. I said what’s he doing? What’s he doing? He says don’t worry, Harry will get the tempo for him. And then Harry would bring me in. But if Harry wasn’t beating the time off I didn’t know what I was doing.…
